NDT training in Farmington, NM: how it works for Farmington employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Farmington technicians and employers is self-paced online theory with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, followed by hands-on practice in person at the employer's own shop or field site. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Farmington. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and the employer certifies. We reply within one business day.

Farmington is an energy town. Gas wells, gathering lines, compressor stations, processing plants and long-distance pipelines spread across the San Juan Basin of northwest New Mexico, and the steel in all of it needs initial weld inspection and periodic checks for wall loss. That makes pipeline and facility NDT the main local market, supported by power generation and general fabrication.

Work in the basin is spread out and often remote. Technicians travel to well pads, stations and pipeline right-of-way rather than reporting to one plant every day, which makes flexible, self-paced theory a practical choice. The hands-on part is then done where the equipment and the procedures really are.

Request a Farmington training quote, and tell us the methods, levels and head-count you have in mind. In Farmington, anyone planning ahead can also read the NDT training FAQ, the Atlantis training overview and the USA training page.

How to get NDT certified in Farmington: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Certification in New Mexico follows the same pattern as elsewhere in the United States. In Farmington, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own technicians, and the standard is a set of recommended practices that each employer turns into a written practice of its own. Here is the sequence in order.

  1. Find or have an employer with a written practice. A technician in Farmington is certified by the company that employs them, so the first step is a sponsor whose written practice covers the method and level you want. In Farmington, the practice sets the hours, the examinations and the recertification interval.
  2. In Farmington, complete the formal training. Take the classroom hours the written practice requires. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method, and your Farmington employer may set higher figures.
  3. Log supervised experience. Document the hours a Farmington technician spends performing the method under a certified Level II or III. Experience is usually the slowest part for a new Farmington technician, so start the log from the first day on a job.
  4. In Farmington, pass the general examination on principles, equipment and terminology for the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the procedures, equipment and acceptance standards your Farmington employer really uses.
  6. In Farmington, pass the practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. In Farmington, pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation at the intervals the written practice sets. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what to expect.
  8. Receive certification signed by your Farmington employer.
  9. In Farmington, recertify at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should not exceed five years, by examination or documented performance as permitted.

In Farmington, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative if you want a credential that stays with you rather than with an employer. Atlantis prepares candidates for that route too. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Farmington technicians

In Farmington, each course follows the body of knowledge in SNT-TC-1A for its method. In Farmington, level 1 courses cover the fundamentals and working under supervision, Level 2 courses cover setting up, calibrating, performing and evaluating examinations to a procedure, and Level 3 preparation covers the basic and method examinations for those who will write procedures and examine others.

Method What the course covers Where it is used around Farmington
UT Sound physics, calibration, thickness gauging, angle-beam weld examination, reporting Wall-thickness surveys on piping and vessels at stations and plants; weld checks on new construction
RT In Farmington, exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretation, radiation safety basics Pipeline and facility welds where radiography is specified; weld acceptance on tie-ins
MT Magnetising methods, field direction, particle application, indication evaluation Structural and pressure-boundary welds, repair areas, lifting and drilling equipment
PT Process control, dwell times, surface preparation, indication interpretation Stainless and alloy piping, small-bore connections, repair welds
VT Acuity and lighting, weld profile, discontinuities, measuring tools, reporting First examination on pipeline and facility welds and on fabricated skids
PAUT In Farmington, focal laws, encoded scanning, data analysis, sizing (UT Level II first) Pipeline girth welds and corrosion mapping where the operator permits phased array
TOFD Diffraction technique, setup, flaw sizing (UT Level II first) Thick-wall pressure equipment welds in processing and power plants

In Farmington, PAUT and TOFD are advanced ultrasonic techniques and are generally taken after UT Level II. In Farmington, whether they can be used on a given job depends on the customer's specification and the employer's written practice.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Farmington

Ultrasonic testing is the workhorse method for gas and pipeline facilities in the San Juan Basin. A Level I course teaches the physics of sound in steel, how to set up and calibrate a flaw detector, and how to take thickness readings. Level II adds angle-beam examination of welds, evaluation against the acceptance standard and reporting. Thickness surveys on piping, separators, dehydrators and compressor equipment are among the most frequent jobs.

Corrosion in gathering and processing systems is often found at low points, bends and under insulation, and a technician who understands where and why metal loss appears gets better data. Practising grid layouts and scanning technique in the Practical NDT simulator builds that judgement. The ultrasonic testing training page lists the course content, and the UT Level 2 practice questions test your theory.

Where NDT technicians work around Farmington

Gas production and gathering. The San Juan Basin has produced natural gas, including coalbed methane, for decades, and operators and their contractors maintain a very large network of wells, gathering lines and facilities around Farmington and Aztec. Operators set contractor qualification requirements, and a documented written practice is typically part of them.

Midstream, compression and processing. Compressor stations, gas treating and processing plants, and transmission pipelines move the gas out of the basin. Pressure piping and vessels there follow ASME B31.3 and B31.8 and API standards, depending on the system, and in-service inspection calls on UT thickness, visual and sometimes radiographic methods.

Pipeline integrity. Transmission and gathering pipelines are regulated federally by PHMSA, and operators run integrity programmes that include excavations, direct examination and weld inspection. Field crews doing coating assessment, weld VT, MT and UT are part of that programme.

Power generation. The Four Corners Power Plant, on Navajo Nation land near Fruitland west of Farmington, is a coal-fired steam station, and plants of that type need boiler tube, weld and pressure-part inspection during outages. Plant ownership and operating plans have changed over the years, so confirm current status when you look for work.

Fabrication and oilfield services. Farmington and nearby towns have skid fabricators, welding shops and oilfield service companies. These shops are often asked by customers to show inspector qualification records as a condition of work.

For earnings information on Farmington-area work, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources. Pay and availability in energy regions follow the activity cycle, so a multi-method certification helps through slower periods.

NDT schools and classes near Farmington: what to compare

If you are searching for NDT schools or classes near Farmington, you will find that the nearest classroom programmes are in larger cities, and many working technicians in the Four Corners therefore choose self-paced theory with practical work at their employer. A fixed-location classroom suits someone who can leave work and travel for a block of days. Online theory suits someone already employed, or a company that wants to qualify field crews without pulling them off the job for long.

Whatever you compare, ask the same questions. Does the provider certify you, or does your employer do that under a written practice? Will your operator or contractor accept the hours? Who grades the practical examination, and are they a Level III? An operator audit of a contractor will read the written practice and the technician's records, so training that fits cleanly into those records matters more than the logo on the certificate.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Farmington. We provide online theory with Level III Q&A and the Practical NDT simulator, and the practical examination is done at the employer's own facility. Our near-me guide covers how to find a sponsoring employer.

Online NDT training in New Mexico

Technicians in New Mexico can take Level I and II theory online at their own pace on the Atlantis portal, with Level III Q&A on the material. Access opens the moment you enrol, which suits crews working long field rotations around Farmington. Practical training and the practical examination are hands-on at your employer's facility, and your employer certifies. See online NDT training and the New Mexico training page.

Online theory covers the classroom portion only. In Farmington, the Level III is available to answer questions while you study, and the portal opens the moment you enrol. In Farmington, courses run year-round, so there is no fixed start date to wait for. Your employer's written practice still decides how many classroom hours count, which is why it helps to ask your Farmington employer before you enrol.

Training a crew at your Farmington facility

A Farmington contractor with several technicians to qualify can run one programme for the whole crew: theory online and self-paced so field work continues, then specific and practical examinations at your shop on your equipment and representative welds and piping. The specific examination can be written around the operator specifications and acceptance criteria your crews actually work to.

If your written practice needs updating before an operator audit, our Level III can help. See written practice development and corporate NDT training, or ask about training a Farmington crew.

For Farmington candidates the practical examination is hands-on with real equipment and specimens and is never conducted remotely. In Farmington, if you want help writing the Level III side of the programme, see outsourced Level III consulting.

Radiography licensing in New Mexico

New Mexico holds NRC Agreement State status, and the New Mexico Environment Department's Radiation Control Bureau regulates radioactive materials and radiation machines in the state. A radiography company needs the appropriate state licence, and individual radiographers must meet the training, examination and supervision conditions in it. Operations on tribal trust land can involve additional agencies, so confirm who has jurisdiction for the specific site. An RT method course does not authorise anyone to use a source and does not license a radiographer. Farmington employers generally need both radiation safety authorisation and SNT-TC-1A certification covering technique and interpretation. Confirm current requirements with the Radiation Control Bureau.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT browser simulator lets a Farmington technician rehearse set-ups, scanning coverage and interpretation in virtual workplaces between hands-on sessions, and the NDT practice tests cover the general and method theory. They are rehearsal tools. They do not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens under your Farmington employer's written practice.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Farmington

How do I get NDT certified in Farmington?

Work for, or be sponsored by, an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its required training and experience, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you.

Is there NDT work in the San Juan Basin?

Yes, in gas production, gathering, compression, processing, pipeline integrity and power generation. Activity follows the energy cycle, so ask operators and contractors directly about current needs.

Can I do NDT training online in New Mexico?

Yes, for theory, self-paced with Level III Q&A. Practical training and examinations are hands-on at your employer's facility.

Which NDT method should I learn first for pipeline work?

Visual weld inspection and ultrasonic thickness are the most common starting points, with magnetic particle and radiography added by many technicians.

How long is UT Level 2 training?

Your employer's written practice sets the hours. The training-requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours; experience usually takes longest.

Do operators accept SNT-TC-1A certification?

Many accept contractor programmes based on SNT-TC-1A, but each operator sets its own requirements. Check what your target operator asks of contractors.

Can I get Level III training from Farmington?

Yes. Level III preparation is online and self-paced with Level III Q&A. See ASNT Level III training.

Does a course certify me?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies. A course provides training and preparation, and ASNT central certification is the alternative if you want a credential not tied to one employer.
